Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:

  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

name: arc-4-reflect-toward-6
description: Use when an ARC grid has a color-4 shape and a separate color-6 marker. Duplicate the 4-shape by reflecting it toward the 6 marker.
---

# Reflect color 4 toward color 6

## Rule
For this puzzle family, keep the original color-4 object, erase the separate color-6 object, and add a reflected copy of the color-4 object on the side indicated by the color-6 object's location. The reflection is across the edge of the original object nearest the 6 marker, so the copy extends away from that edge. Preserve the grid dimensions and all background zeros. The 6 object's exact silhouette is not copied; it functions as a directional marker.

## Procedure
1. Find the connected components of colors 4 and 6; identify the single 4-object and the 6 marker.
2. Compare their bounding-box positions to determine whether the copy goes left, right, above, or below the 4-object.
3. Reflect the 4-object across the corresponding nearest bounding-box edge (equivalently, place an adjacent mirror image on that side). Preserve each cell's offset in the perpendicular axis.
4. Remove all 6 cells; leave the original 4 cells unchanged; paint the reflected cells 4, allowing overlap if applicable.
5. Verify dimensions, bounds, and that no 6 remains.

## Demonstration evidence
- Demo with 4 at rows 0–2 and 6 below: the original was retained, 6 removed, and a vertically reflected 4 copy extended downward.
- Demo with 4 at rows 1–4 and 6 below: copy extended downward by reflecting across the lower edge.
- Demo with 4 at rows 2–5 and 6 to the right: copy extended rightward by reflecting across the right edge.
- Solved instance task-5a83f4b5 had the 6 marker left of the 4 shape; the correct output removed 6 and added a horizontal mirror of the 4 shape to its left.

## Pitfall
Do not rotate the 4 shape, do not replace it with the 6 silhouette, and do not merely extend/copy the 4 shape without reflection. Check the side indicated by the marker; the copy is a mirror image, not a translation.",
